title: Coverage Limits per Covered Person under Payment Protection
content:
Coverage limits under Payment Protection apply per covered person, across all of the borrower's plans.

## Provisions

1. **Covered principal.** The unpaid principal covered for one person across plans may not exceed the largest unpaid principal a plan covers (USD 50000.00). Fees are charged, and death benefits paid, only on principal up to that amount, taking the older loan first.
2. **Month limits.** Lifetime limits on disability and unemployment benefit months are counted per plan and claim type. A benefit month that would exceed a per-claim or lifetime limit is not paid.
3. **End of the plan.** Reaching the lifetime limits of every covered event ends the plan, with the reason recorded as maximum benefits paid.

## How the quantities are counted

| Quantity | What is counted | As of |
|---|---|---|
| Principal covered for a person | the total unpaid principal of the customer's loans that have a Payment Protection plan in enrolled or active status | today |
| Benefit months on a claim | the monthly benefits paid on that claim that have not been reversed | the life of the claim |
| Lifetime benefit months | the monthly benefits paid on the plan for claims of the same claim type (disability, or unemployment) that have not been reversed | the life of the plan |

A reversed monthly benefit does not count toward either month limit. Disability months and unemployment months are counted separately; one never uses up the other's limit.

## Hypothetical allocation of the covered principal

The loan figures below are invented for illustration; the cap is the largest unpaid principal a plan covers, USD 50000.00.

A borrower holds two personal loans, each with a Payment Protection plan in active status: an older loan with an unpaid principal of USD 30,000.00 and a newer loan with USD 35,000.00. Their total, USD 65,000.00, is above the cap. Taking the older loan first, all USD 30,000.00 of the older loan is covered; the newer loan is covered for the USD 20,000.00 that remains under the cap. The other USD 15,000.00 of the newer loan's principal is not covered: no fee is charged on it and no death benefit is paid on it.

## Hypothetical month count

A disability claim has received monthly benefits for as many months as the per-claim limit, one of which was later reversed. The reversed month is not counted, so the claim stands one month below the limit and the next qualifying month is paid. Without that reversal the claim would stand at the limit, and a further month would not be paid.
